item.title: [Translation] Cursor Case Study: 800+ PRs a Month, or How to Build Trust in AI Agents for Development
item.description:
The webinar summary below is part of a closed intensive course I put together around a series of webinars from the Maven platform about AI cases in American big tech. First, we watch a live stream with practitioners from Cursor, Meta, Netflix, and similar companies, and the next day, we discuss it in a small group. We don't watch adapted educational English, but the live speech of people who are currently building products on agents, and we extract vocabulary and life hacks from it. The webinar from which I made the article was conducted by Lauren Tan from Cursor. The webinar topic is trust in AI agents in development: how to reach the point where agents merge PRs without your involvement (about a built verification system). Below is a summary for those who want to understand the case in Russian. Enjoy :-) Read more

item.title: Who Actually Broke Your AI Agent: The Model or the Harness?
item.description:
When an agent in production makes a mistake, the team's discussion goes in circles: "the model is dumb," "the prompt is flawed," "the API is to blame." A recent study from Scale AI assigns blame for failures to the edge between components and the fault side. It turns out that "the model is to blame" almost never means "fix it with fine-tuning": I break down a taxonomy of 41 failure modes, a catalog summary, and four of my own failures with numbers – none were resolved by changing the model. Read on.

item.title: How to configure Arch Linux to outperform Windows 11 in performance and style
item.description:
Working with Linux often scares beginners, but it's unnecessary. Linux is not a difficult system; it's just different. To work with it comfortably, it needs to be configured. My name is Valery Linkov, I am an expert in security, clouds, and networks, and a mentor for cybersecurity courses at Yandex Practicum. In this article, I will explain how to turn a basic, inconvenient Linux into a powerful system that surpasses Windows 11 in performance and style. Don't believe me? Then follow me.

item.title: What Prevents AI from Becoming a Full-Fledged Work Tool: Outcomes of the "AI Without Illusions" Meetup
item.description:
Those implementing AI have a new headache. The more a technology can do, the harder it is to figure out where to apply it. A chatbot just needs to answer a user's request, but an agent can already be given access to a browser, corporate documents, code, and other tools. And with this, it's no longer enough to ensure the model is smart. You also need to prove that it solves a specific task, fits into the process, and doesn't bring new risks. This was the focus of the "AI Without Illusions" meetup. Experts analyzed corporate AI from various angles – from finding real human benefit and early agent scenarios to internal tools and their implementation across an entire organization. Read more

item.title: On-device OCR for primary documents: how to recognize documents without sending them to the cloud
item.description:
Imagine a common situation: a forwarder accepts goods at a warehouse, signs an invoice, and photographs the document with a corporate smartphone. Within seconds, the details should appear in the accounting system – without manual data entry, an office scanner, or waiting for the paper to reach accounting. But there's a condition: the photo must not be sent to an OCR provider, a third-party processing center, or a manual verification operator. Ideally, the image never leaves the mobile device – only the extracted and verified data enters the corporate system. Is it possible to recognize a multi-page UРD (universal transfer and acceptance document) with a complex table on a smartphone, correct perspective, read small print and handwritten notes – all without connecting to external infrastructure? The short answer is yes. However, for a secure primary document recognition system, it's not enough to write "works locally" in a presentation. The entire document workflow must be properly structured – from the smartphone camera to 1C or ERP. Read more

item.title: How to connect Google Calendar and Google Drive to an agent or Why is everything so complicated
item.description:
I'm writing this article because I spent quite a bit of time figuring out how to connect Google Workspace services to Claude Code CLI and OpenClaw. And I want to make it easier for others. I've tried to explain what's happening so that when you read your agent's instructions or documentation, you understand what they want from you. The article doesn't contain a step-by-step guide to setting up a specific client. It's a collection of knowledge on how to set up any client (e.g., one written by your agent). Connecting an agent to calendar and mail is a useful topic. I can't imagine scheduling meetings for many people manually anymore (though I have Vietnam flashbacks =)) Read more

item.title: AI Agents' SDD: How We Re-invented a Very Fast Waterfall
item.description:
Let's consider a typical product task. We need to add a new feature. The team describes it using Specification-Driven Development, defining scenarios, constraints, APIs, and acceptance criteria. An agent receives the context and quickly writes code, tests, and infrastructure. Within a day, or even sooner, the result is almost ready. But where's the waterfall in this? If the feature is isolated, the team can safely roll it out under a flag, quickly see user feedback, and just as quickly roll back the change. Then, a large agent batch becomes an excellent experiment. Hello, Habr! My name is Marat Kinyabulatov, I'm an expert in agile practices and responsible for the efficiency of engineering teams at the core of the bank. In this article, I'll discuss when SDD truly helps agents and when it prematurely locks in a solution. I'll illustrate this with several cases and explain how to maintain a short feedback loop when code appears faster than the team can verify the results. Read on
